why:
rcl's installable log handler. We ship one; the SIGNATURE differs, and the constraint that makes it differ is the FFI mirror rule.

OURS: `rclc_log_sink_fn` + `rclc_log_add_sink(sink, user_data)` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/log.h`, phase-417 W4.d). It APPENDS, so a consumer teeing records to its own transport does not discard whatever the board installed, and records raised before any sink existed are replayed into the first one installed.

THE DIVERGENCE: rcl's handler takes a `rcutils_log_location_t *` STRUCT (file / function / line) plus a timestamp. Ours takes the same information as FLAT ARGUMENTS — `(user_data, severity, logger_name, logger_name_len, message, message_len, file, file_len, line, timestamp_ns)` — because cbindgen skips the logging module, so a struct crossing this FFI would be HAND-MIRRORED, and a mirror that misses an appended field passes a SHORTER struct than the reader reads. That is issue 0160's class, which has bitten three times. With flat arguments an appended field changes this TYPE, so every sink fails to COMPILE instead of reading stack garbage. Name and message are pointer+length rather than NUL-terminated for the reason `c:logger_get_name` states: the Rust side holds a length-delimited `&str`.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13). This was a `gap` asserting two things, both now false. (1) "a C or C++ caller cannot install a sink and must instead implement the `nros_platform_log_write` ABI in a board crate" — `rclc_log_add_sink` landed in W4.d. (2) "the C emit path hardcodes `file: \"<nros-c>\", line: 0, timestamp_ns: 0`, so every record from a C or C++ call site reaches the sink with no location and no time" — `rclc_log_emit_at` / `rclc_log_emit_fmt_at` carry file and line, and the timestamp comes from `nros_log`'s own `__timestamp_ns()`, so C records are stamped by the same clock as Rust's (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs`); `<nros-c>` survives only as the value for a caller that passes no file.
